name: Bimetric-Khronon Slip MOND (BKSMOND)
claimed_mechanism:
This architecture utilizes Hassan-Rosen bigravity to exit the DC-013 slip-lock: the second metric $f_{\mu
u}$ carries the independent off-ray lensing slip ($\eta 
eq 1$) sourced by the MOND force law, while the physical metric $g_{\mu
u}$ follows the MOND potential. A khronon $	au$ is introduced to mediate the PPN preferred-frame response (fixing $\alpha_1, \alpha_2$), with its coupling to the acceleration $a_\mu$ screened by $e^{-y}$. Crucially, the kinetic normalization of the khronon (its mass and sound speed) is controlled by an independent Bekenstein-Stelle-like constant, decoupled from the $e^{-y}$ screening coefficient, thereby resolving the P7 collision (screening that kills kinetic normalization). The MOND force law is realized via a constraint on the physical metric's extrinsic curvature, with $f_{\mu
u}$ acting as a slip carrier.

The preferred-frame PPN parameters $\alpha_1, \alpha_2$ are proportional to $e^{-y}$ (vanishing in the Solar System) and are determined by the khronon's independent kinetic parameters, not the screening factor, ensuring no strong-coupling divergence as $y 	o \infty$.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-001 (local no-preferred-frame lensing) because it explicitly includes a khronon (preferred frame) and a second metric (multi-sector). It is inequivalent to DC-010 (finite-alpha_inf khronometric) because the PPN coupling is screened by $e^{-y}$ (not constant) and the kinetic normalization is independent (not controlled by the screening factor, avoiding P7). It is inequivalent to DC-014 (stiff/non-propagating vector) because the slip carrier is a dynamical second metric (Hassan-Rosen), not a stiff vector, and the khronon is propagating (standard kinetic). It is inequivalent to DC-002 (AeST) because the preferred-frame coupling is screened by $e^{-y}$, not a constant $K_B$. It is inequivalent to DC-012/DC-013 (frameless localized nonlocal) because it includes a preferred frame (khronon) and a second metric.
